title: Wills, estates, and advance care planning

verified.claim: Assets properly placed in a living trust pass to beneficiaries without probate; probate typically takes at least 9 months.
verified.quote: When you die, as long as you have put your assets into the trust, they should go to the beneficiaries without having to go to probate court. ... The fastest that can happen in California is typically 9 months

title: When formal probate may not be needed

verified.claim: Property held in a living trust is outside the probate estate; simplified procedures exist for small estates and, since 2025, for a main home worth up to $750,000.
verified.quote: A new law in 2025 raised the limit for real property to $750,000, but only if it was the person's main home in California.

title: Probate Code § 16061.7 (text as amended by AB 976, 2017-2018)

verified.claim: When a revocable trust becomes irrevocable at death, the trustee must notify beneficiaries and heirs; they then have 120 days to contest.
verified.quote: When a revocable trust or any portion thereof becomes irrevocable because of the death of one or more of the settlors of the trust ... "You may not bring an action to contest the trust more than 120 days from the date this notification by the trustee is served upon you or 60 days from the date on which a copy of the terms of the trust is delivered to you during that 120-day period, whichever is later."

verified.claim: The trustee's notification is due within 60 days of the death.
verified.quote: The notification by trustee shall be served not later than 60 days following the occurrence of the event requiring service of the notification by trustee
